about.what: What this operator PC needs to know about the slots it drives: the drawing server, ROS settings, per slot whether it is mounted, its force sign and its real-time core, the touch, the collision thresholds. Which robot hangs in which slot, its address and its DDS domain are the site table's (site_table), one source for each fact.
about.mounted_source: 2026-10-02: the arms under control are 2R and 3R (site/aris_2026-10.json live_note). Set `mounted` true for a slot only when its arm hangs there and answers on the site table's address.
about.force_sign_note: per slot: +1 when the paper pushing the pen up reads positive; -1 on the hung (inverted) arms, as found 2026-10-06. The first `aris touchoff <slot>` from the planning PC checks it: its report shows the sign of the force onset.
about.slots_note: arms are slots 1L 1R 2L 2R 3L 3R (DESIGN 4c); the old robot ids live on only in the site table
about.rt_core_note: each mounted slot's stack runs pinned to its own isolated core (`taskset -c rt_core`, 16-19); link drops ended on 2026-10-07 once each arm's loop had its own core, with the NIC's IRQs on cores 12, 13, 32, 33 (README, a one-time host step). Real-time priority is set on the control-loop threads only, by the site's helper (README), never on the whole launch: that froze the PC. 3L (the floor arm) and 3R (empty) get none: their robots are never driven.

ros.joint_prefix_note: joint names are <joint_prefix>_joint1..7; the briefing notes one stack that used fr3v2
ros.hardware_component_note: the ros2_control hardware component of franka_description's fr3 ros2_control xacro; recovery brings it back (inactive, then active) after the reflex is cleared

touch.source: the calibration touch under position control (DESIGN section 6 step 1; orchestrator 2026-10-01)
touch.cap_note: above the air zero at any reading: the arm stops where it is and holds; no way back is flown until a person has looked
touch.extra_note: a touch motion may go on past its planned end by its extra_depth, at most extra_max, at extra_speed
touch.field_note: on the arms 2026-10-06/07: onset 3 N over 15 readings, cap 6 N; the detector arms only at constant descent speed (a trip in the descent's own acceleration is not a contact)

collision.source: set for a job (not a mark job) and restored after it, as the old stack raised them before every pass (control-stack briefing 2026-09-09 section 9: 20 N -> 40 N; HARDWARE_DAY1 1.5: the installation operator's 40/40/36/36/32/28/24 Nm, fr3drivers' 'sensitive' 20 Nm / 20 N). Lower and upper thresholds, acceleration and nominal, all set to these.
collision.force_n_note: the Cartesian thresholds: x, y, z in N, then the three torques in Nm

desk.source: Franka Desk's web API for the calibration driver (desk.py). panda-py has no call for the operating mode; this request is sent through its authenticated helper with Desk's control token.

mode_endpoint.note: found on the hardware 2026-10-06 (FR3 system 5.9): POST /desk/api/operating-mode/programming or /execution, empty body, header X-Control-Token: <the control token>, 200 OK. Every Desk call is a row with its HTTP status; if Desk changes, copy the request from the browser's developer tools here.

execution.source: what worked on the arms, 2026-10-06 (field report). The start tolerance is the job header's or rig.json execution.start_tolerance_rad (0.03), not here.
execution.settle_note: after a move the arm counts as standing still when every |qd| <= rest_qd; joints are read after at most settle_s of waiting for that

auto_recover.note: a link drop is recovered by itself, once per every_s per arm; any other fault waits for a person (aris recover on the planning PC)

execution.stale_note: a joint reading older than this is no reading: rows say q null with 'stale joint states (last x s ago)'
execution.fresh_note: after a recovery the joint states must be fresh again (their stamp advancing over 1 s) within this, else serve restarts the arm's stack and checks again

gripper.source: the old working parameters (Aris_Kindt arm_orchestrator/arbiter.py), 2026-10-07: open to 70 mm at 0.10 m/s; close = a grasp to 0 mm at 0.10 m/s with 70 N, epsilon inner 0, outer 80 mm
gripper.check_note: open when wider than open_noop_m is a no-op; after every command the width is read back, and jaws that moved less than min_move_m fail (libfranka reports success for a grasp that moved nothing)
